title: Introspective kernel scorer + lazy-cast coalescer for quant-friendly decode/prefill
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Dequantization and precision transitions (INT8 <-> FP16/FP8) produce measurable CPU and kernel launch overhead during both long prefill sequences and low-latency decode. Existing routing picks a single path per-model or per-request without looking at runtime signals which causes suboptimal choices when sequence lengths or KV cache patterns vary.

Goal: Implement an "introspective" kernel scoring layer in the runtime that evaluates candidate kernel execution paths (INT8, FP8, mixed-precision FP16) using lightweight online heuristics (sequence remaining, kv-hit ratio, batch composition, device memory pressure) and chooses the path with the best expected cost-latency tradeoff. Pair this with a "lazy-cast coalescer" that defers and coalesces dequant/cast operations across contiguous KV entries and streaming decode micro-batches to reduce redundant conversions.

Scope: runtime kernel selector + small changes to prefill scheduler and KV cache layout. No upstream model changes. Implementation spans: selector scoring function, lazy-cast coalescer that hooks into KV write/read, micro-batch aware decode loop integration, and perf regression tests and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Selector correctly picks INT8/FP8/mixed kernels for >95% of sampled traffic in canary compared to offline oracle decisions
End-to-end p95 token latency for prefill workloads (8k mean sequence) reduced by >=15% vs baseline when using INT8-friendly paths
Decode tail latency (p99) not increased by more than 5% for small-LLM low-latency workloads
Reduced number of distinct dequant operations per request by >=30% on streaming decode traces (measured by cast/op counters)
Feature gated rollout with telemetry showing per-region token throughput, GPU util, CPU overhead, and cost-per-1M-tokens; no regressions in error rate or memory OOMs
comments: 2025-03-10 - Aisha K: Kickoff. Design doc created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Introspective+Kernel+Scorer (draft). Key idea: cost model + simple ML-style shim that uses current batch composition and device stats.

2025-03-11 - Jonas M: Prototype scoring function implemented in runtime/kernel_selector: uses weighted features {seq_remain, kv_hits, batch_sz, device_free_mem, quant_mode_penalty}. Running microbenchmarks on A100-80GB and Intel-GPU emulators.

2025-03-12 - Eng review by Priya S: Suggest adding a hysteresis window to avoid thrashing between FP16 and INT8 for long-lived sessions. Also flagged security_review_required for new instrumentation accessing device metrics.

2025-03-13 - Jonas M: Added lazy-cast coalescer. Instead of performing dequant per KV read, KV writes annotate contiguous ranges with cast-state and a coalescer applies a single vectorized dequant. Early microbench: 24% fewer memcpy + 12% lower CPU usage for streaming decode traces.

2025-03-14 - Perf team (benchmarks): End-to-end tests on 8k prefills: INT8 path + coalescer = 18% p95 reduction vs baseline mixed-precision runtime. Small-model decode p50 unchanged, p99 +3% (within threshold). Need additional checks on memory fragmentation.

2025-03-15 - PM review (Lena R): Approve canary rollout in staging region. Prepare telemetry dashboards and rollback criteria. Add docs for ops about new feature flag runtime.kernel_selector.introspective.
Next steps: finalize gating, add unit tests for cast coalescer correctness (edge cases when partial KV entries overlap), run longer soak in staging for 72h with high-variance sequence lengths.
